changed_reading.after: It is a controlled routing table of judgment: a common liability is realized through materially distinct directions and media.

seeds.focus_anchor: The four وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ clauses: أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِبًا, أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ, خَسَفْنَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ, and أَغْرَقْنَا.

changed_reading.after: The ayah stages exact distributive liability: all are within judgment, but no case loses its own deed-to-consequence pairing.
changed_reading.before: All the named peoples were punished for sin.

seeds.focus_anchor: The fronted فَكُلًّا, the singular possessive in بِذَنۢبِهِ, and the repeated وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ.

changed_reading.after: The clause supplies the causal topology of the whole ayah: self-directed misplacement precedes and is exposed through literal displacement, without making God its wrongful source.
changed_reading.before: The closing clause only denies divine injustice and blames the victims.

seeds.focus_anchor: The contrast وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ.

changed_reading.after: 29:40 also reads as the visible result-sheet of the surah's opening assay: conduct under pressure becomes legible in differentiated outcomes.
changed_reading.before: 29:40 reports punishments imposed on already identified wrongdoers.
